text: Git branching is a powerful feature that helps teams manage changes to their code without disrupting the main project. When working on a new idea or fixing a bug, developers create a **feature branch**—a separate copy of the code where they can experiment freely. This keeps the main branch stable. Once the work is complete, a developer creates a **pull request** to propose their changes. Team members can review the code, leave comments, and suggest improvements before approving it. Finally, the branch is **merged** into the main codebase. This **version control workflow** ensures collaboration is smooth, reduces conflicts, and makes it easy to track every change made over time.
